brief: A crowded potting-bench corner fills the image: a leaning stack of damp terracotta pots furred with moss, a rusted trowel, and a snail mid-crawl on a rim. Behind them, foxgloves, lupins and hollyhocks melt into a soft, out-of-focus wall of lilac and rose madder. Rich layered watercolour carries the background bloom, while the foreground is built with dry-brush and coloured pencil for the gritty clay and slick snail trail. Dappled, overcast English light gives no hard shadows. It feels humid, overgrown and tenderly specific.

A halved red cabbage, its cut face filling the frame, is rendered with microscopic fidelity but mapped into a false-colour space-telescope palette. The dense leaves glow amber and gold, the veins turn teal, and the cavities sink into magenta and inky blue-black. Fine spray builds the gaseous gradients, and dense stippled points scatter like stars along the outer edge into a black void. Sharp pen detail keeps every crinkle botanically exact. The effect is cosmic and scientific, a kitchen vegetable read as a deep-field nebula.

A single glossy aubergine lies on a black lacquer tray. Its skin is rendered so precisely that the window reflections curve across it like liquid, and the green calyx is fuzzy and exact. The ground is a deep, layered black built from charcoal mass and dark glazes. Fine gold dust is sprayed in drifting clouds across the tray, and a few hairline gold pen tendrils follow the tray's rim. Palette: lamp black, aubergine purple-black, persimmon highlights and burnished gold. It feels hushed, precious and ceremonial, a vegetable treated as heirloom.

A close three-quarter view of an old motorcycle's V-twin engine, rendered with the look of a wet-plate tintype. The palette is chocolate black, pewter and creamy silver, with nothing else. Dense charcoal mass builds the shadow, and soft graphite picks out the cooling fins, oily bolts, braided cables and a cracked leather seat edge in hyperreal detail. Focus falls off sharply into swirling blur. The plate edges show uneven collodion pour marks, comet streaks, and a dark vignetted border where the emulsion thinned.

Sliced citrus wheels of blood orange, lime, pink grapefruit and lemon are packed edge to edge, seen straight down. The white pith walls between segments read as raised gold cloisonné wires, drawn with thin, gleaming ochre pen. Each juice cell is hyperreal, with glistening vesicles, tiny seeds and moist highlights, yet the colour fills sit flat and glassy like polished enamel. The palette is intense coral, chartreuse, carmine and citron. The tiling is dense and edge to edge, with no background visible.

An open vintage leather suitcase stands alone on an endless cracked salt flat, and a calm ocean pours out of it toward the horizon, Surrealist in logic. Every element is hyperreal and drawn in dense, burnished coloured pencil: worn tan leather, brass clasps, a striped lining, polygonal salt crusts, and tiny waves foaming at the lip. The sky is a smooth gradient from Naples yellow to pale cobalt. The vanishing point is set low and off-centre, and long raking shadows give the scene a hushed, impossible stillness.

A swirled resin bowling ball fills the frame like an antique celestial globe. Its marbled burgundy and teal surface is rendered hyperreal, with deep translucent swirls, three finger holes, and a scuffed lane polish. Over it lies a fine engraved overlay of constellation figures, meridian lines and star dots drawn in thin sepia pen. Everything sits beneath a yellowed amber varnish glaze with craquelure. A brass meridian ring arcs around the ball in perspective. The lighting is a warm museum spot from above.

A Haitian tap-tap bus roof is piled high with cargo against a flat turquoise sky, in the dense, joyous spirit of Haitian naïve painting. The scene includes stacked plantains, bundled sugarcane, woven baskets, crated hens and a bright tarp. Each item is rendered hyperreal, with bruised plantain skins, feather barbs and rope fibres. The perspective stays naïve and flattened, with objects stacked upward and no single viewpoint. Saturated marker colour fills the scene in vermilion, emerald, cobalt and banana yellow. The painted bus panel below carries ornate hand-lettered borders, but no words.

A fanned hand of playing cards lies on green baize, drawn hyperreal with worn corners, a bent queen and baize nap. The image is built from four separate hatched pen layers in cyan, magenta, yellow and black, each slightly shifted out of register. Coloured fringes therefore ghost every edge, pip and face card. Up close it reads as overlapping cross-hatch screens, while at a distance it becomes almost photographic. The cards are cropped diagonally with the card fan breaking the frame.

A tabby cat sleeping on a cast-iron radiator, depicted as a colouring-book page caught mid-work. The left side remains crisp, uniform black pen outlines on bright paper, with simple closed shapes and empty interiors. Toward the right, the same lines vanish under obsessive hyperreal coloured pencil: individual whiskers, ginger and grey fur, chipped cream radiator paint, and a sock drying beside the cat. The boundary between outline and finish is ragged and abrupt, so the drawing reads as an obviously unfinished page.

The side of a rural shed is patched over decades from mismatched materials, composed like a Gee's Bend quilt. Improvised offset blocks combine corrugated tin, faded barn-red boards, a teal door panel, a strip of feed-sack sign and weathered plywood. Each patch is hyperreal, showing nail heads, peeling paint, galvanized spangle and grain checks. The joins are slightly crooked and the strips run in bold, uneven bars. The view is frontal and flat, filling the whole sheet, under bright, even daylight.

A ribbon of honey falls from a wooden dipper and folds into coils on itself. It is rendered hyperreal, with refracted amber light, trapped bubbles, and a liquid skin that mirrors the window. Around it the canvas erupts in lyrical abstraction: broad sweeping watercolour gestures in raw sienna, saffron and burnt umber, misted spray veils, and loose calligraphic marker arcs that echo the pour's rhythm. The precision of the subject floats inside joyful, improvised colour weather. The space is off-kilter, with the dipper entering from the upper left.

A row of homemade preserves on a kitchen sill, backlit and arranged inside a pointed lancet arch like a Gothic window. Each jar is hyperreal: raspberry ruby, damson violet, apricot amber, with bubbles suspended in the jelly, gingham lids, and handwritten labels curling at the edges. Heavy charcoal-black outlines act as leading, splitting the glass into jewel-like cells. Transmitted light makes the fruit glow from within, while the jar rims catch sharp white glints. Watercolour is glazed in many layers until it deepens like pot-metal glass. The composition is strictly vertical and symmetrical.

Freshly dyed lengths of linen hang over a wooden ladder in a dim workshop, still dripping. The cloth is hyperreal, showing a weighty wet sag, crinkled folds and droplets at the hem. Diagonal arashi pole-wrap resist lines streak each panel, rendered in layered watercolour indigo, from deep Prussian to pale woad blue, with white ghost lines left in reserve. Faint green oxidation tints the edges still turning. A stained vat rim crosses the foreground, and soft side light rakes across the cloth.

A tight crop of a worn denim jacket lapel with a single enamel pin of a saguaro cactus fastened through it. The twill is drawn hyperreal in diagonal indigo pencil hatching, with fades, a frayed buttonhole, a copper rivet and stray lint. The pin has flat sage and sunset-pink enamel fills, gold die-struck borders, a tiny scratch, and a reflected window highlight. There is a slight pucker where the pin's post pulls the fabric. The light is a soft overcast daylight with a shallow depth of field.

A single hyperreal pear sits large on a flat mustard-ochre field, in the manner of a Polish film poster. A brass keyhole is cut into its flank, and inside it a tiny, perfectly rendered staircase spirals down. The fruit is modelled with subtle russet freckles, a bruised blush and a stalk with peeling bark, and it contrasts with a crude, hand-scrubbed gouache-like ground. Rough crayon edges, deliberate imbalance and generous empty space create the image. The metaphor feels witty and slightly ominous, and there is no text.

A hyperreal butterfly-stroke swimmer bursting from turquoise water. Droplets, goggle strap and straining shoulder are rendered in exact, slick marker gradients. Then the frame glitches. Rectangular blocks from the previous instant drag diagonally through the body, so a smeared slab of chlorine-cyan water slides across the swimmer's face. A streak of skin-tone pixels bleeds sideways into the lane rope. Flow-field streaks carry colour along the corrupted motion vectors in hot magenta and acid lime chroma noise. The block edges stay razor-sharp against the soft photographic passages. The composition is horizontal and cinematic, like a broken broadcast still.

Two smoked mackerel lie on crumpled newsprint beside a heel of rye bread, every scale, gold-bronze skin sheen and flaky crumb rendered hyperreal. They are framed inside a bold carved woodcut border of thick black gouged lines, folk scrolls and a lettered banner. Flat stencil-dabbed colour in crimson, saffron and leaf green is laid loosely over the border and slips out of register. The hyperreal centre and the naive printed frame clash deliberately. The paper is coarse and greyish, and the ink sits heavy at the outlines.

A hyperreal hinged aluminium sculpture of interlocking planes stands on a raw concrete floor, half-unfolded like a creature mid-movement. Each plate is rendered with exact brushed-metal reflections. Some faces are painted flat cadmium orange and egg-yolk yellow, others left bare grey. Hinges, rivets and edge burrs are crisp. Graphite and soft charcoal build the floor's pitted texture and the overlapping cast shadows. The background is an empty, pale gallery wall. The composition is off-centre, inviting the viewer to imagine folding it.

A yellow rubber dishwashing glove is draped over the edge of a sink against a wall of hand-painted tiles. The glove is rendered photographically: wet sheen, wrinkled fingers, droplets. The tiles carry cobalt and manganese-purple sketches of windmills and a tiny ship, executed with loose, dragging, pooled watercolour brushwork. A fine network of glaze crazing runs across the tin-white surfaces in pen hairlines. Grout lines are drawn with exact soft shadows. Cool kitchen light picks out a single drip running down a tile.
